subtitle: Fall Star Testing, Candidates tab, both schools shown (the widest case: the second line carries the school). Today the roster picks its tablet columns from the window’s width, so with the side panel taking 72 px (Standard) or 96 px (Largest) the Candidate and Testing for columns get squeezed to 40–60 px and text runs into text. After (v1.053, built per v1.130): const narrowRoom = usePageRoomBelow(640); const stacked = isPhone || narrowRoom; for the roster only. Limit: 640 px of room. Below it the roster draws the phone’s stacked rows (the ones phones already show); at 640 and above nothing changes. Dialogs, ⋯ menus and the rest of the page keep following the window.

columns.note: How the limit was measured. The real roster in preview, touch, admin, details shown, both schools (the widest case), Panel size Largest, window 640–1024 px in 1–8 px steps; for each width: the room (the page area’s own data-page-room), text boxes of two cells of one row that overlap, and cells whose text is wider than the cell. Text over text stops at room 617; text sticking out of its column stops at 636 (632 still has 6); 640 is the first clean round number above both and the same as Dashboard core’s sample (parts.html#L02/room). Standard gives the same results at the same room (the room is what counts). With a mouse the actions column is 24 px narrower, so the roster is clean from about 616: 640 covers both. One school selected and Hide private details need less room. PC columns (1024+) are clean at 1024 with Largest (room 928). Your call if you want more: at room 640–695 the tablet columns are clean but tight (names on 4–5 lines, “Testing for” header on 2 lines); from 696 they look exactly as at 820 (the approved tablet). A limit of 696 would also stack 700 / 720 / 760-wide windows with Largest.

footer:
Unchanged

How the pictures were made. Star testing · rolling check pass 2, L-02. Preview screenshots (fake database, admin, Fall Star Testing, “Show both schools”), Panel size set through the Account menu. Today = the app as it is. After = drawn on the real page by mock-room.js: the phone roster’s own markup was copied from the app at a 600 px phone window (same event, same rows) and put in place of the tablet roster at each target size. Its styles (.st-crow-c.is-phone, .ev-srow-main …) are not behind a phone-width rule, so they draw as they will once the roster follows a class. So the rows are exactly the phone’s; what a copy can’t show: buttons don’t work in the drawn roster, and the tablet page around it (summary cards, Dan switch, top bar) is today’s — which is also what the change keeps. Nothing in the app was changed. Amber = text over text, or text sticking out of its column.
